messages:
Mia (Marketing): OK team — we need a lightweight playbook for field + SDRs to use vs cloud AI platforms and the infra vendors. Goal: one-pager + 3 quick scripts + a webinar hook. Can we iterate quickly?
Jamal (Growth): +1. Need to call out predictable latency, cost controls, and simple migration path. Short bullets.
Priya (Sales): Real reps want objection-handles: 'why not just use managed endpoints from cloud X?'
Theo (Field Ops): For enterprise buyers, latency SLOs and private deployment are the big wins. Also mention dedicated capacity commits.
Alex (MktOps): I can draft the one-pager. Sam, can you give numbers from the latest benchmarks to justify the claims?
Sam (Research): Quick numbers: median p99 for our dedicated runtime = 85ms (open model, 8k context) vs cloud-managed ~200-450ms in our tests. Cost per 1M tokens after batching optimizations: our SKU = $420, top cloud vendor-managed = ~$1.1k (similar model class). I'll share raw result links.
Mia (Marketing): Perfect — can we make those soundbite-friendly? e.g., '3x lower latency at half the token cost' — but check math.
Sam (Research): Safe soundbite: '~3x lower latency, ~2.5x lower cost in production workloads we tested.' I'll attach the experiment ID.
Priya (Sales): Need short scripts for SDRs: 1) quick inbound, 2) technical buyer, 3) procurement.
Mia (Marketing): Draft scripts: 
- SDR inbound: "We help teams cut inference spend and reduce tail latency — can I share a one-pager that compares unit economics vs managed endpoints?"
- Technical buyer: "Our runtime keeps KV cache across bursts and gives predictable p99s; we also support private VPC deployments and can run on your infra."
- Procurement: "We offer reserved capacity and usage-based hosted plans — both with clear metering and enterprise SLAs."
Jamal (Growth): Add an inbound routing rule: any lead mentioning 'latency', 'cost', 'SLA', or 'private' -> auto-route to AE queue X and flag for field enablement. Alex, can you add that to the webhook?
Alex (MktOps): Yep. I'll add a Zapier rule + a CRM tag. Will also include a 'webinar attendee' auto-tag.
Theo (Field Ops): Webinar hook idea: "How we got predictable p99s on mixed workloads" — do a short live demo of failover to cheaper model variants. Field can co-present.
Mia (Marketing): Love it. We'll market it as a 30-min technical session with a 15-min demo + 15-min Q&A. Date target: 3 weeks out.
Sam (Research): Legal note: we can share anonymized benchmark numbers but no direct competitor screenshots. Create a benchmark appendix for attendees. Eve, any concerns?
Eve (Legal): Anonymized aggregates are fine. Avoid 'customer X uses Y' statements unless we have permission. Also avoid direct pricing comparisons that claim vendor pricing errors. Keep phrasing like 'in our tests' and include methodology.
Priya (Sales): For the one-pager, can we include 2 customer scenarios: startup PLG app & enterprise search pipeline? Those map to hosted + private deployment pitches.
Mia (Marketing): Good call. I'll draft one-pager and short A/B lines for SDRs. Jamal — can you run an A/B test on the SDR subject lines?
Jamal (Growth): On it. Two variants: 
A) "Reduce inference cost and p99 latency — quick one-pager"
B) "Predictable LLM inference: reserved and private options"
I'll track open->demo conversion.
Alex (MktOps): Routing config done (staging). I'll push to prod after Mia signs off on language.
Mia (Marketing): Timeline: Drafts by EOD tomorrow, legal signoff in 48 hours, webinar assets + invite by end of week.
Theo (Field Ops): Field slide deck ready for review. I'll drop it in the shared drive.
Sam (Research): Posting experiment links: https://redwood-internal/reports/bench-2026-llm-inference (anonymized). Use the 'methodology' slide.
Priya (Sales): One more objection handle: 'We use provider X's managed offering because of integrations.' Response: "We support same integration points + SDK parity and can run in your cloud/VPC so no lock-in risk."
Mia (Marketing): Nice. I'll weave that into the one-pager.
Eve (Legal): And add a small footer: 'Benchmarks were run on models A/B/C with synthetic and customer-proxy workloads; individual results may vary.'
Mia (Marketing): Great. Thanks everyone — I'll circulate the draft and drop a CTA for review. :thumbsup:
Priya (Sales): Thanks — will prep prospect list for webinar invites.
Jamal (Growth): I'll queue the A/B test and report back.
Alex (MktOps): Dropping routing PR after copy lock.
Theo (Field Ops): Ready to co-present.
Sam (Research): Happy to present methodology.
Eve (Legal): Standing by for final copy review.
